findings.summary: expand() recurses into the last expanded word, which includes the last file path. A check input whose path contains the literal text {files} (e.g. tests/{files}.mjs) with any template using {files} recurses forever: "Maximum call stack size exceeded" and startup stops with exit 1 (receipt spec-05-r2-probe.log). Fix: recurse only into the template suffix, e.g. expand the suffix first and join its first word to the last file.
findings.assumption: A check path containing the placeholder text is not a realistic input, so this does not fail spec-5-1; the coordinator may treat it as blocking since it is in the changed code.

findings.summary: A root or check path that itself contains $( ; | or && is single-quoted and runs correctly as printed, but the printed string still matches the spec's literal forbidden regex, so a text-based guard may refuse it. The spec's check uses ordinary paths.
findings.assumption: Paths with shell operators are outside the spec's intent.

findings.summary: templateWords treats $VAR, backticks and && in tests.focused as literal text and the printed command quotes them ('$VAR', '&&'), so an env-var reference in a template no longer expands. Unquoted backslashes are POSIX escapes, so node C:\tools\run.js becomes C:toolsrun.js. A whitespace-only template yields the files alone as the command. An unclosed quote throws and stops startup with exit 1, while a broken joycraft.yaml is otherwise swallowed (line 216); a note like spec-5-3's would be gentler.
findings.assumption: The spec does not decide template syntax beyond {files}; literal words are the safer reading.

findings.summary: Windows-style inputs are not reachable through startup on POSIX: a worker root containing backslashes fails before Joycraft code runs (Node ERR_INVALID_MODULE_SPECIFIER loading the entry script), and backslash or drive-letter check inputs are refused by the existing path validator. shellQuote output is POSIX single-quoting, which cmd.exe/PowerShell do not read the same way; a native-Windows paste was not tested.
findings.assumption: Pre-existing behavior outside this spec; POSIX shells are the target.
